description:
Tex Taylor was named "Prairie Kid".

Tex Morgan was named "Red Hawkins" in this issue.

Canine Cupid, When the feud between their fathers prevents Bingo and Samantha from seeing each other, Rebel comes up with a way to bring them back together.

Change of Heart, Mr. Wilkin, up to his ears in tax forms, is in no mood to give Bingo money for a date; But his mood changes after another confrontation with Samson Smythe.

Girl Watcher one-page story, Li'l Jinx notices that Greg is following her, but can only guess why.

Painful Lesson, Mr. Wilkin tries to get Mr. Smythe to stop calling him "Wilkins" instead of "Wilkin."

See Saw, Bingo and his friends go to the Smythe house to play their music for Samantha; Teddy tries to do something "dastardly" to break up Bingo and Samantha, and only Rebel can stop him.

To Stretch a Point, Teddy tries to make his move on Samantha while Bingo becomes obsessed with playing paddleball.

The Big Broadcast, Uncle Herman re-wires the Bingoes' sound equipment, giving them a better sound but accidentally broadcasting them to every radio and TV in town.

Treasure Hunt, Bingo tries to win Mr. Smythe's undying gratitude by saving his life.

Air Your Gripes, Mr. Smythe organizes a pro-environmental demonstration at City Hall, and inspired by his activism, the Bingoes show up at the protest to help the cause with their music.

The Vicious Cycle, Mr. Smythe uses Teddy's motorcycle to show off his cycling ability, only to be one-upped by Uncle Herman.

A Day in the Life of a Fool, Bingo vows that by the end of the day Mr. Smythe will love him like a son; Filled with typical Wilkin stubbornness and stick-to-itiveness, he spends the entire day ignoring Samantha and trying to make her father like him.

The Beat Goes On, Everyone keeps mistaking Buddy's incessant drumming for the sound of something breaking.

The Old Pro, Uncle Herman bores everyone with stories about his past as a professional baseball player.

All Aglow, After Bingo trips on one of Mr. Smythe's barbells and crushes his guitar, he and Samantha have an argument and break up, to her father's joy.

Fiddler's Choice, Mr. Smythe and Teddy try to prove that Uncle Herman is lying about having been a professional baseball player.

Night Shades, Teddy is proud of the fact that his dark glasses are his exclusive trademark, until the Wilkins get hold of a whole case full of shades.

The Man and the Boy, After a handsome doctor saves Mrs. Smythe's life, Samantha decides to transfer her love from the immature Bingo to the mature, wise doctor.

Split, Bingo decides to drop out of school and go out on the road on his own; Rebel follows him and is hit by a car.

Muscle Milk, Teddy thinks that drinking Mr. Smythe's mixture of yak milk and charcoal has given Rebel super strength.

Wanted Man, After Mr. Smythe is heard yelling "Oh, dad blast the dad blasted dad blast," everyone yells at Uncle Herman for getting Mr. Smythe mad.

Business Is Picking Up, Teddy gets the Bingoes a gig playing at a benefit against littering.

A Moving Tale, Sampson has a new business opportunity and is moving his family away from the neighborhood, to the despair of Samantha and Bingo.

Neighbors, After Uncle Herman tosses him a garbage-covered baseball, Mr. Smythe threatens to sell his house to an unsuitable new neighbor.

Note: Archie Andrews, Betty Cooper, Veronica Lodge and Sabrina Spellman make non-speaking cameos in the story, "Business Is Picking Up".

It's All So Involved, Bingo meets a boy who's run away from home and decides to help him, despite Samantha's warnings against getting involved with other people's troubles.

Bully For You, Mr. Smythe won't let Samantha play in Bingo's group with long-haired sissies, so the Archies come up with a plan to make him think that long-haired musicians are actually strong.

The Fourth Man Theme, When Buddy is sick, Samantha recommends her brilliant musician friend Matt Turner as a replacement.

Part of the Family, When no one in the Wilkin household wants his help, Uncle Herman decides to pack up and leave.

A Private Affair, Samantha gets a beautiful new dress for her first formal party, one of the most important experiences of a young woman's life—only to find that Bingo has broken his arm and can't go with her.

My Country 'Tis of Thee, Mr. Smythe complains that today's dances are too wild and untamed, and demands to see a dance that's quintessentially American.

The Protector, Samantha uses her martial arts skills to protect Bingo from a bully, while making Bingo think he's the one doing the fighting.

The Final Inning, Uncle Herman falls off a ladder and goes into a coma. Bingo and his friends play music under his hospital window to try and revive him.

A Wild Stretch!, Miss Grundy teaches about the history and uses of rubber.

Honest Injun!, Mr. Smythe is once again furious with Bingo, until he has a dream that Bingo is the first astronaut to travel to Venus.

The Heart Doesn't Lie, Samantha tells us the story of how her father tried to push her away from Bingo and toward Teddy, and how her mother managed to set things right.

Mood Madness, As part of his homework for an acting course, Bingo has to be churlish and unpleasant for four hours, followed by four hours of nonstop smiling.

Mr. Smythe's Clean Scene, Outside a chemical factory, Mr. Smythe finds his daughter, Bingo and Teddy protesting against pollution, leading to an argument about environmentalism, picketing, and the dangers that big business is inflicting on the planet.

How's That Again?, Dilton teaches his friends about the picture game known as a Rebus.

There's Something About a Soldier, After Bingo passes his army physical, Mr. Smythe, Bingo and Teddy argue about draft-dodging, which Mr. Smythe considers un-American. Bingo and Teddy defend the people who refuse to fight in an immoral war, but finally agree that if they're drafted, they'll go and fight even though they oppose the war.

Separate Lives, Bingo and Samantha decide they should date other people.

No Respect, Mr. Smythe makes fun of the new generation's wild new threads.

That Silly Backbone, Bingo goes to get revenge after Samantha is brutally beaten by a couple of thugs.

The Ghost Hunters, Bingo, Samantha and Teddy go to a ski lodge that has few customers because everyone thinks the house next door is haunted; The intrepid trio decides to find out what's causing the spooky noises in the house.

Can You Top That? Li'l Jinx plays William Tell with a boomerang instead of an arrow.

Who Do You Trust, Mr. Smythe, decrying the current trend toward permissiveness, warns Samantha not to start any wild parties in his house while he's away; Soon after he leaves, a school bus full of young children breaks down in front of the house, and Samantha lets the kids in while it's being repaired.

Heartache Is a Two-Way Street, In a story narrated by Samantha, she takes Bingo for granted, running around with many exciting boys and keeping Bingo on a leash for when she needs him; When Bingo gets tired of this treatment, Samantha fixes him up with her plain friend Sally, who can keep him occupied without being a threat to Samantha.

My Selfish Heart, Samantha narrates the story of how she felt Bingo wasn't paying enough attention to her and started to transfer her affections to Teddy, only to find that Teddy was a cad.

A Moving Scene, Mr. Smythe becomes furious when he learns that a Japanese-American family is moving into the neighborhood, and starts a petition to get them kicked out.

Fairy Tales Can Come True, Uncle Herman claims to have a date, but Willie and Mr. Smythe follow him and discover that he's actually following a pretty nurse home from work without having the nerve to talk to her.

Enemy Action, The feud between Mr. Wilkin and Mr. Smythe causes them to ban their families from visiting each others houses.

Rebel Rouser, Teddy realizes that Rebel acts human when no one else is around except him; Teddy tries to convince the others that Rebel is "bewitched."

Weight and See, Bingo is depressed because Samantha is so much stronger than he is, so she tries a trick to boost his confidence.

Camera Angle, Teddy tries to get photographic proof that Rebel is no ordinary dog.

Now Hair This, Samantha tries to prevent Bingo from seeing her with her hair in curlers, but he thinks she's hiding because there's a prowler in the house.

Between Two Loves, When Rebel gets sick, Samantha demands that Bingo choose between her and the dog, and Bingo chooses to break their date and stay behind with Rebel.

Easy Come Easy Go, Mr. Smythe mocks the lottery as a waste of time, and when he gets a free ticket, he gives it to Bingo.

It's Ladder Than You Think, Mr. Smythe sees a report on television that Bingo and Samantha have eloped and that Bingo plans to sponge off his new father-in-law.

Help From Beyond, A mysterious old lady tells Bingo that there's a fire at the Smythe house.

Responsibility, Mr. Wilkin tells Bingo to call off his date with Samantha so he can stay home and help paint the house.

The Bees Are For the Birds, Mr. Smythe is furious when he learns that there's a sex education course in Bingo and Samantha's school; He's even more furious when Mr. Wilkin and Uncle Herman don't share his belief that sex education is for "liberal minded pinkos."

Mum's the Word, Mr. Smythe complains that today's generation has no gumption or backbone, but then Bingo saves his life.

Strong Finish, Bingo declares that he's breaking up with Samantha because he can't bear the shame of everyone knowing she's stronger than he is.

Of Crime and Punishment, \When Uncle Herman insists on going for a walk alone at night, everyone is afraid that he'll get mugged.

It's Your Move, When he sees all the Smythe furniture being loaded onto a moving van, a despairing Bingo stows away on the van so he can find out where Samantha is moving.

Phantom Strikes Again, After Mr. Smythe throws him out again, Bingo asks Buddy to deliver a note to Samantha.

Journey Into Jeopardy!, Bingo has an extra-sensory premonition that the Smythes' car trip will end in disaster, so he sabotages their car to keep them from going.

The Start of Something Big!, Bingo is flattered when Mr. Smythe trusts him with the key to his house.

The Banning of Bingo!, When Samantha's grades go down, Mr. Smythe assumes it's because she's been seeing too much of Bingo, and forbids them to see each other until her grades improve.

Some Changes Made, A snooty interior decorator comes over and tells Mr. Wilkin that everything in his house will have to go, much to Mr. Smythe's amusement.

The Busy Body, Mr. Smythe is upset that everyone is whispering when he's around, and demands to know what's going on behind his back.

Taken For Granite, When Bingo accidentally breaks Mr. Smythe's "America: Love It Or Leave It" statue, Sampson thinks it was broken on purpose and chases the "liberal-minded pinko" Bingo away from his house.

Up, and at 'Em one-page That Wilkin Boy story, Mrs. Smythe asks Bingo to wake up her husband.

Thick Thinking starring Li'l Jinx, Charley is going on a trip to New York.

My Case Rests one-page That Wilkin Boy story, Mr. Smythe tells Bingo to set up a hammock.

The Moment of Truth, When Bingo hears that a new boy at school insulted Samantha, he vows to find the guy and make him apologize, until he learns that his adversary is a karate expert.

The Good Old Daze, After complaining about how much everything costs now due to soaring '70s inflation, Mr. Smythe attends an "Old Tyme Fair" where everything is at turn-of-the-century prices.

The Rivals, Jealous of Bingo for monopolizing his little girl, Mr. Smythe tries to get her attention and then kicks Bingo out of the house again, which causes Samantha to refuse all her meals for a week.

Muscle Bound, Suddenly Bingo has so much strength that he can lift any barbells without trouble, while the Smythes are weak by comparison; Or is this all a dream?

Male Call, Sampson says that Samantha has been seeing too much of the wimpy Bingo and that she should date some boys who are more muscular and aggressive.

Hero, The sexy and wily Dimples Delush tries to seduce Bingo away from Samantha, but just as Bingo is about to succumb, Mr. Smythe inadvertently foils her plan.

Daddy's Little Grown Up, After Samantha insists she's not a kid any more, Mr. Smythe overhears her and Bingo talking about "tying the knot."

Giant Killer, Bingo goes to sell a lawnmower and all he comes back with is a handful of beans, leading to a dream where Mr. Smythe is the giant at the top of the beanstalk.

Teacher, Mr. Smythe nurses an injured bird back to health, but still manages to disprove Uncle Herman's theory that he's really an old softy.

The Old Crab, Samantha tags along with Bingo when he goes crabbing.

A Date To Remember, Bingo double-dates with Teddy and a couple of fast, thrill-seeking girls.

Quiet Please, Wanting to work at home in peace and quiet, Mr. Smythe shoos a bunch of little kids away from his house, but winds up missing their noisiness.

Love Thy Neighbor, At his mother's insistence, Bingo reluctantly leaves Samantha with Teddy and goes to welcome the new neighbors; They turn out to be a beautiful widow who lost her husband in Vietnam, and her equally beautiful teenage daughter, Zelda.

The Weak Spot, Mr. Smythe suspects everyone of trying to scam him, even little girls selling Girl Scout cookies; His suspiciousness leads to him being scammed by a phony policeman.

Gift of Gab, When Samantha sees Bingo going shopping with Zelda Maxson, she decides to fight for her man by butting in on their date.

That Old Feeling, Both Bingo and Sampson scoff at Samantha's premonition that something bad is going to happen tonight.

Enemy Action, The Wilkins go to a movie. The Smythes are there too, and Mr. Wilkin and Mr. Smythe start feuding again, until both families are kicked out of the theatre.

Generation Gasp, Uncle Herman gets a visit from his fun-loving old buddy Charlie, an obnoxious jerk who won't stop talking.

Slice of Life, After watching a soap opera about a young girl who marries an old man, Mr. Smythe suspects Samantha is about to do the same thing in real life.

The Fencing Problem, Bingo's dad tries to get Samantha's dad to stop leaning on his fence.

Merely Magnificent, Sampson gets in big trouble with his wife when she hears him refer to Samantha as "a mere woman."

Mad, Mad World, Though Mr. Smythe mocks Rebel as a pathetic excuse for a dog, when Smythe and Bingo are confronted by muggers it's Rebel's quick thinking--and a little whipped cream--that saves the day.

Perfectly Clear, When Bingo can't hit any of Samantha's pitches, former pro ballplayer Uncle Herman tries to give him some pointers.

Blossom Time, Mr. Smythe enrages his wife when he ridicules the idea of a husband bringing flowers to his wife. To make amends, he tries to get her some flowers, but for as little money as possible.

Power Mad, To cope with the energy crisis, Sampson insists that his wife disconnect the washer and dryer and start washing clothes by hand.

That's Love, Samantha accuses Bingo of not being willing to do enough to prove his love for her.

Health and Happiness, Mr. Smythe goes out jogging early in the morning and everyone is woken up by his grunting.

The Beat Goes On, Buddy plays beats that have a hypnotic effect on Bingo and Teddy.

Generosity, Bingo's group The Bingoes comes over to the Smythe home to practice; Teddy continues to be obsessed with proving that Rebel acts human.

Charade, When Teddy tries another scheme to get Bingo away from Samantha, Rebel goes to Samantha to warn her.

Dad's Dilemma, Mr. Wilkin wins Mr. Smythe's respect by proving he can lift weights through sheer force of will power; Samantha reveals that her father calls her "Sam" because he wanted a boy, while her father starts to think that Bingo might make a good father for his grandson.

Drum Rolls and Coffee, Buddy goes to pieces after Mr. Smythe takes away his drumsticks; The gang tries to find him something else to drum with.

Love Is Where You Find It, Bingo and Samantha try to convince their dads to stop their feuding and learn to love each other.

Struck Out, The devious Teddy tries to break up Bingo and Samantha by sending Bingo over to Zelda Maxson's house.

What's Your Bag?, Bingo's dad won't let him go out until he cleans up his room.

Name Game, Mr. Smythe offends Bingo by repeatedly making fun of his nickname.

Triple Play, No matter where Bingo takes Samantha to try and recite love poetry to her, Teddy turns up to mock Bingo for his mushiness.

The Gift of Friendship, When Samantha asks Bingo not to get her a birthday gift, he takes her at her word; But when he shows up at her birthday party without a gift, she yells at him for being a cheapskate.

Remember the A La Mode, Samantha bakes an apple pie, and Bingo goes out to get some ice cream so he can eat the pie "a la mode."

A Women's Lib-Rib, Bingo is depressed because Samantha is so much stronger than he is, so Uncle Herman suggests challenging her to some games that he can beat her at.

Girl Power, Tired of going with a girl as freakishly strong as Samantha, Bingo threatens to dump her for some girl "who wobbles and jiggles like real soft girls do"; Samantha resolves to win Bingo back by tricking him into thinking she's become a weak, helpless female.

The Hero Game, Teddy spends the day showing off for Samantha by flaunting his superiority to Bingo at physical feats; When Teddy climbs up a tree to save a cat, Rebel sees his chance to turn the tables on Teddy.

Strength Is Power, Bingo is appalled to find that even his parents have accepted the idea of equality between the sexes; He starts making speeches about how men are the superior gender because of their superior strength, until he gets another reminder that his own girlfriend could easily beat him up.

Now or Never, Mr. Wilkin worries that Bingo and Teddy's constant use of teen slang will leave them unable to speak in normal English; Samantha shows Mr. Wilkin that he has nothing to worry about.

Man, Oh Man, Tired of Mr. Smythe constantly insinuating that he's unmanly, Bingo resolves to show Samantha's dad that he's the most macho of macho men.

Choice of Weapons, Samantha is thrilled when Bingo and Teddy decide to fight a duel over her; She's less thrilled at their weapons of choice: marbles.

Mail Call, Bingo sends Samantha a package in the mail, even though they live next door to each other; Samantha thinks it's romantic while her father and Teddy think it's ridiculous.

Energy Crisis, When Samantha comes over to visit the Wilkins, jumping and bouncing all the way, her boundless energy leaves the whole family exhausted just from talking to her.

Love Struck, Rebel falls in love with a cute French poodle who breaks his heart.

Network Nonsense, Mr. Smythe is driven crazy when everyone around him starts speaking entirely in catchphrases from TV commercials.

So Black, So Blue, No one will believe Teddy when he says he got a black eye when he "walked into a door."

A Date With Disaster, Teddy repeatedly tries to sabotage Bingo's date with Samantha.

A Note of Trouble, Bingo is rattled when he finds a threatening note pinned to his door with a knife.

Weather or Not, Bingo and Samantha make fun of their fathers' faith in old wives' tales and wise old sayings.

Dog Gone, When Teddy makes fun of a seriously ill Rebel, the dog is restored to health through his sheer hatred of Teddy.

The Inner Man, Samantha tries to help Bingo get over his inferiority complex about his lack of strength, but she fills him so full of confidence that he thinks he can take on a big hulking bruiser.

The Artful Dodger, Bingo uses ballet training to become a better football player.

Dig That Snow, Teddy gets a snow plow and uses it to ruin Bingo's attempts to shovel the walk.

Trick Or Treat, Bingo tries to teach Rebel to do tricks, but as usual, Rebel will only show his true abilities in front of Teddy, just to mess with his mind.

Dummy Up, Bingo goes into hysterics at the thought of being seen carrying a dress-maker's mannequin through the neighborhood.

Just a Minuteman, Samantha tries to organize a Bicentennial pageant, but gets no cooperation from the guys.

Play it Again, Who?, Samson takes steps to insure he doesn't have to listen to the loud rock music the teens favor.

Council of War, Samantha is thrilled that Bingo and Teddy are fighting over her, if she can get them to actually fight.

Josie appears in the Hostess advertisement.

Photo Finish, Bingo cons Teddy out of a date with Samantha.

Balance of Power, Bingo's efforts to make less work for himself end up making more work for himself.

War Games, Willie and Samson lock horns again and their wives decide to intercede.

I Sing the Songs, Samson tries to teach Bingo how to properly serenade.

A Slight Hitch, After Rebel chases a bone into the back of a delivery truck, Teddy braves all obsticals to bring him back.

Women's Work, Bingo and Samantha decide that she should handle delicate stuff--like dealing with muscle-bound Romeos at the beach.

See Sick, After Samson forbids Bingo from seeing Samantha, Bingo starts dating her blindfolded.

Rebel Power, After witnessing Teddy's dirty trick on Bingo, Rebel decides to get even.
Deserted Village, The kids get away from the neighbors by going to the beach.

The Obstacle Course, Teddy's booby traps, intended to embarrass Bingo, snare the adults instead.

Disaster Area, Bingo's clumsiness decimates a department store.

War of the Words, Teddy and Bingo argue the merits of equal rights for women.

Space Story, To help Samson feel better about his small den, Bingo paints scenes on the walls to make it seem bigger.

The Protectors, Bingo and Teddy's dispute over Samantha gets rough and spills over onto Samantha.

Work of Art, Bingo gives Samantha a portrait of his Civil War era ancestor, who happens to look just like him.

What a Waste, Teddy tricks Bingo into burrowing through garbage.

The Rebel Yell, Rebel falls in love with a french poodle and goes missing from the Wilkin home.

Balance of Power, Teddy tries to set Bingo up by getting him to balance two of Samson's prized glasses.

Tease for Two, Samson and Willie spend the afternoon arguing across a fence.

Flaming Nuisance, Samantha and Teddy heckle Bingo when he tries to make a point about the United States.

Teddy Takes a Tumble, Teddy shows off his gymnastic moves to humiliate Bingo.

Rebel Rouser, Bingo doesn't want to put Rebel in a kennel for the duration of their vacation any more than Rebel wants it.

Split Personalities, The fence between the Smythes and the Wilkins falls down and Willie can't afford to replace it.

Club Disaster, Bingo runs down to the gym to pass a message on to Samson.

Rebel's Revenge, Rebel takes protracted revenge against Teddy for a prank he played on Bingo.

Board to Death, Bingo keeps getting in trouble with the tough guys on the beach.

A Better Batter, Mr. Smythe is sure that Bingo hit a baseball through his window even after everyone else tells him it was Uncle Herman.

Service with a Smile, The boys try to score points with Mr. Smythe at the beach, but he takes advantage of their good deeds.

Star Struck, The boys come over to watch the game on television, but Mr. Smythe wants them to keep the noise down.

Daddy's Little Girl; Samantha is annoyed because her father treats her like a child; Later, he overhears her talking to Bingo and believes they are talking about getting married.

Paper Doll, The neighborhood is upset because their newspapers have not been delivered, and Bingo and Teddy try to help out when they discover the reason why.

Winged Victory, Mr. Smythe makes fun of the bird house that Bingo built, so Uncle Herman offers to help out.

Real Gone; Bingo needs to get a message to Samantha but her father is so angry with him he can't get near her house.

Oven Ready, Samantha becomes convinced that Wilma hates her.

Ruled Out, Bingo has a new job as a park ranger, so Samson has to go and heckle him.

Pitcher's Battle, Bingo tries to teach Samantha how to pitch.

Very Charming, Teddy tries to sell Bingo some jewelry.

Give Till It Hurts, No one particularly likes Mrs. Smythe's artistic creations made from seashells, but no one will tell her, either.

A Mynah Problem, Mr. Smythe buys a mynah bird and teaches it to insult Mr. Wilkin, so Bingo comes up with a way to turn the tables.

A Game of Chance, Bingo and Uncle Herman put in a shuffleboard court and Mr. Smythe is determined to spoil it somehow.

Sacrifice Play, Uncle Herman decides that he's just in the way and leaves the Wilkin house, so Bingo has to come up with a way to make him change his mind.

It Takes a Thief, After Bingo is rushed to the hospital, Samantha meets and falls for his doctor, and signs up as a volunteer.

What Are Friends For?, A jealous nurse, Jessica Jason, tries to frame Samantha for robbery; When that doesn't work, Jessica makes Samantha think Bingo is unfaithful.

What's In a Name?, Samantha is followed home from the hospital by two mysterious, threatening-looking men.

Silence is Golden, After finding out that the men are undercover cops, Samantha tries to help them catch a crook at the hospital.

The Conspirators, Mr. Smythe tries to keep his wife from finding out that he and the Wilkins are planning a surprise birthday party for her.

Shopping Spree, In preparation for Mrs. Smythe's surprise party, the Smythes and Wilkins go shopping for presents.

The Secret, Teddy mistakenly thinks that the surprise party everyone is preparing is for him.

Party Boy, Mr. Smythe's yells at his wife to keep her from finding out her surprise party, making her so angry that she leaves him and never shows up for the party.

Sporting Gesture, Samantha is accused of stealing money from the hospital's charity tennis tournament.

The Fall Guy, Bingo and Samantha discover who really stole the money and turn the thief in, but then they find themselves in another bad situation.

Reflexes, Bingo accidentally hits a pedestrian who later claims to be more injured than his tests would indicate.

Sink or Swim, Bingo exposes Keith's scam.
Last Issue!

Record Release, The Bingoes play a gig at Harvey's Headache, a discotheque that got its name because the owner can't stand the music.

Special Delivery, Samantha asks Bingo to accept delivery of a package that she doesn't want her father to see.

As Luck Will Have It, Teddy convinces Bingo that one of the trinkets he's wearing is actually a cursed Egyptian scarab.

The Magic Square, Mr. Smythe and Mr. Wilkin get Bingo out of his hippie garb and into more conservative clothes; Then Bingo finds out what Mr Smythe wears when he attends a meeting of his Lodge.

Come To the Fair, After Rebel causes him to smash his guitar, Teddy tries to get enough money to buy a new one by setting up a kissing booth at the fair.

Untitled one-page story, Flower Child, a new and short-lived character, claims that her new coat is a "maxi-coat."

Nice Try Spy Guy, Teddy tries to exploit Samantha's jealousy of Bingo's gorgeous guitar teacher, Gladly Divine.

Think Session, Sampson won't let Samantha study at the new youth center when he finds it's full of loud, blaring music and teenage chatter, but she can't study in the deafening silence at home.

side note: racist Li'l Jinx comic

High Test Heartbeat, When the engine in Teddy's car develops a rhythmic knocking sound, Buddy literally falls in love with the engine knock.

The Real Thing, Teddy gets a thoroughbred dog, and both he and Mr. Smythe tease Bingo about the new dog's superiority to Rebel.

Delayed Action, Teddy plans to make time with Samantha while Bingo is in the next town running an errand for her father, but something always prevents Bingo from leaving.

Caught In the Middle, Bingo and Samantha break up, to the approval of their fathers, but their mothers decide to get them back together again.

Inventing We Will Go, When Bingo wins a TV set, Uncle Herman tries to re-wire it so it will get 3-D picture.

Along Came Bingo, Bingo and Samantha rent a motor scooter to go on a picnic.

The Master Stroke, Rebel decides to get the jump on Teddy by clobbering him before he perpetrates a foul deed against his master.

Love Thy Neighbor, Mr. Smythe gets Bingo out of his hair by sending him on an errand to the health food store.
